clues: This city in the south of Zambia lies a short way north of the Zambezi River. It stands close to one of the great falls of the world.
Wet months here are hot and rainy, and the time just before them turns very hot. Dry months stay mild, with cool nights after warm days.
In 1911, this city became the first capital of Northern Rhodesia. It kept that high role till the year 1935.
This place takes its name from a Scots man who roamed and taught the faith. He was the first man from Europe to roam this land.
Most guests come for the great falls a short trip from this city. Those falls are the main draw for guests from near and far.
